tone_statements.quote: Tone. Muji-PJZ has five contrastive tones 55, 33, 13, 21, 52 [...] Some varieties possibly feature a 22 contrast, but this pitch value usually only surfaces due to sandhi in Muji: /21/ > [22] / __ 21 unless three 21 tones are in succession in which case /21, 21, 21/ > [22, 21, 21] or [21 22 21] depending on the variety. MLT /a³³nɯ²¹ma²¹/ ‘monkey’, for example, is pronounced [a³³nɯ²²ma²¹], and QLC ‘weave’ /jɛ²¹kʰə²¹/ is pronounced [jɛ²²kʰə²¹] until preceded by another /21/ tone such as the 3S pronoun /ɛ²¹/; this combination is then pronounced [ɛ²²jɛ²¹kʰə²¹] ‘s/he weaves’.

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2011. A Phula Comparative Lexicon: Phola, Phuza, Muji, Phowa, Azha. SIL Language and Culture Documentation and Description 18. Dallas: SIL International. 144 pp.
sources.note: Silent. Sec. 3.3 'Southern Muji phonology in brief' pp. 8-9 (PJZ, not Qila): {(C)(V)VT} template, five pitch contrasts, [22] sandhi allotone, tense voice and nasalization non-contrastive. Qila Muji only on the clade list/map (p. 3) and in sec. 4.6 subgrouping. Zero hits for 'stress'/'accent' in the full text; refers readers to Pelkey (2011, De Gruyter: 223-270) for fuller sketches.
sources.venue: SIL Language and Culture Documentation and Description

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority (submitted by Jamin R. Pelkey). 2007. Request for New Language Code Element in ISO 639-3: [ymq] Muji, Qila (associated Change Request 2007-120). SIL International. 5 pp.
sources.note: Nothing (identity/location only: autonym Muji; alt. names Doka, Mujitsu, Phutsu; primary village 'Qila'; c. 1,500 people; two-three isolated villages of southern Jinping County plus reportedly one village in Lai Chau, Vietnam; closest language 'possibly Bokha').

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-120 (split [ymj] into [ymc] Southern Muji, [ymx] Northern Muji, [ymq] Qila Muji, [ymi] Moji, [ymz] Muzi). SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing; notes [ymq] shares c. 60% core lexical similarity with Southern Muji and scored.38 on a Southern Muji recorded text test.

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2007. Muji's mirrored merger: correlative redistribution of checked tone classes in a newly defined Burmic cluster. Mon-Khmer Studies 37: 179-195.
sources.note: Silent. Sec. 2 'Sample phonology sketch' (pp. 181-183) describes Southern Muji (PJZ): syllable C(V)VT, 34 initials, five tones 55/33/13/21/52, sandhi, non-contrastive phonation. Qila Muji (QLC = 'Muji: Qila village, Jinshuihe district, Jinping county', key p. 194) appears only in tone data: a /21/-sandhi example p. 183, /52/ reflexes for 'hard','cold' p. 185, Tables 3-7. No occurrence of stress/accent anywhere.
sources.venue: Mon-Khmer Studies: A Journal of Southeast Asian Linguistics and Languages 37

tone.says: Muji cluster lects (incl. QLC) carry lexical tone written with Chao numerals; the sample sketch lect PJZ has five contrastive tonemes 55, 33, 13, 21, 52 (52 marginal, often a sandhi allotone of 21/55/13), 13 realised [213]/[212]/[313]; a [22] pitch surfaces by sandhi /21/ > [22] / __ 21, illustrated for Qila Muji with 'weave' /jɛ21 kʰə21/ > [jɛ22 kʰə21] and 's/he weaves' [ɛ22 jɛ21 kʰə21] (p. 183); phonation is non-contrastive, a feature of tones 21 and 13; QLC 'hard' and 'cold' keep a /52/ refl…
